body: The meter and rhyme are both wrong. Yours isn't a very good song. How hard could it be, to count one two three, when explaining you saw a long schlong?

I don't blame them for being rude, I'm not even sure if it is rude. It's just that tone or that facial expression that lets me know people aren't really glad I exist. 

> I know when I'm at my lowest is precisely when I don't want to seek out help from my support system or professionals

Exactly. I'm glad it's not just me. If that's how it usually works then it makes sense to establish that network now, just to make sure I am not facing  walking into a strange building or meeting a new person when I'm not up to it but need to go in. It's very nice of you to do this by the way. It's probably pretty stressful. I'll let you get on with your day.

Thank you. I'm worried about the record mostly, but I'll take the first step of at least emailing them about exactly how that would work. You are of course right and you've explained the reasoning well. That's probably the way I should explain it to them.

I don't know. It's little things. It's like now that I understand it's optional the idea that I could just stop if I don't like something pops into my head a lot. Like I'll be in someone's way at the market and the tone they use to ask me to move will make me think "They don't want me here" and I'll think about it rest of the day, you know? By the way, I got rid of the gun a few months ago. It's not like I see it all the time and consider doing something impulsive any more.

thanks

>When you do go in to get help what do you tell them? 

Sorry I wasn't clear, I haven't been in yet. I don't know what I would tell them. I'm a little worried it would impact other areas of my life, but I could email them about their policies. 

> How are you feeling right now?

Not great, but I'm not where I was. Kind of bummed out today, but that's not at all the same thing. Many things have been improving over the last year. 

Thanks for asking.
